dependent_variable.name: MBE
dependent_variable.definition: Indicator equal to one when forecast error (actual EPS minus the median consensus forecast, divided by beginning-of-fiscal-year stock price) is nonnegative while adjusted forecast error is negative. The paper specifies the median consensus forecast closest to the earnings announcement and I/B/E/S actual EPS from the Historical Summary tape for forecast-error calculations. ADJFE is NDEPS minus the median forecast; NDEPS equals actual EPS minus discretionary accruals per share (equivalently, cash flow from operations plus nondiscretionary accruals per share). Thus positive discretionary accruals allow the firm to cross the forecast threshold. Zero otherwise.
dependent_variable.formula: 1{FE ≥ 0 and ADJFE < 0}; FE = (actual EPS − median forecast) / beginning-of-year stock price; ADJFE = NDEPS − median forecast; NDEPS = actual EPS − DA per share.

TA is operating income after depreciation (Compustat178) minus cash flow from operations (308); PPE is net property plant and equipment (8); DeltaREV is change in annual net revenue (12); DA is the fitted residual. The source says all variables are scaled by average total assets for the year. The display has two substantive predictors and an ordinary constant; no inverse-assets predictor is printed, and the scaling sentence does not explicitly say that the intercept is scaled. Estimated cross-sectionally by two-digit SIC industry and year; delete the top/bottom1percent of total accruals and cash flow from operations per industry-year; exclude industry-years with fewer than8observations. Do not supply a familiar three-predictor Jones variant. COORDINATOR-VERIFIED MATHEMATICAL TRANSCRIPTION (Nondiscretionary EPS and adjusted forecast error, physical PDF page 8): NDEPS = Actual EPS - Discretionary accruals per share; equivalently Cash flow from operations + Nondiscretionary accruals per share. ADJFE = NDEPS - Median consensus analysts forecast. These are deterministic transformations, not extra estimated regressions.

models.results_reason: Supporting-model results are outside this campaign.

review_notes: The principal family is Table 4 pooled full-sample columns 1 and 2: both directly test the auditor-tenure/meet-or-beat question using the authors’ two stated tenure parameterizations, Equation (2) with continuous tenure and its square and Equation (3) with short/long indicators. The pre-/post-SOX columns are H1a partitions and later forecast-error/discretionary-accrual sensitivity tests are excluded.

Equation (1) is retained as the required supporting Jones fit because its residual DA is used to calculate NDEPS, ADJFE, and MBE. The verified reading transcription confirms only PPE and ΔREV as substantive predictors plus an ordinary constant; all variables are scaled by average assets, with no statement that the constant is scaled.

The Jones estimator is not identified. Table 4 reports two-way cluster-robust inference for cross-sectional and time-series dependence but does not name cluster identifiers. The model includes two-digit SIC industry indicators, but the research-design definitions say 52 while the Table 4 note says 53 industry codes.

The HORIZON definition for the main model (months to earnings announcement) differs from the Table 2 descriptive note (months to fiscal year-end). The Table 3 variable definition referenced by Table 4 is used for the baseline, with the timing difference retained as an unresolved source issue. SHORT is defined as >1 and <4 in Equation (3) and as 3 years or less in the appendix; excluding first-year engagements makes the definitions equivalent for the retained sample.
The per-share conversion of the Jones residual DA for NDEPS is not reported, so the source does not fully specify this outcome construction.
results_review_notes: The selected frozen baseline family is the full-sample pooled Table 4 columns (1) and (2). Pre-SOX and post-SOX columns (3)–(6), later cutoff tests, and other robustness analyses are outside the selected baseline family.

Table 4 reports industry and yearly indicators as included and explicitly states their parameter estimates/statistics are not reported; this is retained as a result-set note rather than treated as a missing substantive predictor.

Table 4 reports coefficients and z-scores, states z-scores use two-way cluster-robust standard errors, and defines two-tailed significance markers. Standard errors and normal-reference p-values are derived from the printed z-scores under the conventional zero-null coefficient Wald relation; markers remain source-specific bounds.
Table 2 forecast-horizon descriptives use fiscal year-end as the starting date, whereas the Table 3/Table 4 model definition uses earnings-announcement date; the descriptive link remains unclear.

The Table 1 Panel C “% of firms” header is retained literally alongside observation counts; its denominator convention is unresolved. Table 2 absolute discretionary-accrual and absolute forecast-error rows are not direct inputs to the retained MBE definition and are not linked. The Table 3 Pearson correlation matrix is excluded as a correlation table, not a descriptive summary.

The source labels the Table 2 ratio as net income/average total assets (ROA), while the model variable definition says income before extraordinary items/average total assets; preserve the source wording in the descriptive-row note.
